subject: Org ignition: admin invites, API tokens, and KMS handoff
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Roberts <amelia@streamlinehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Org ignition: admin invites, API tokens, and KMS handoff

Hi Amelia — great to be live on this kickoff. A quick note to align the first milestones so our implementation sprint is predictable: 

1) Admin invites: Monica will send the initial admin invites for your team (owner, infra, security). Please confirm the two people you want as org owners.
2) API tokens & projects: we recommend creating one project/environment for your PoC and a service token scoped to read/write for the model route. Marcus will seed a sample token and rotation notes.
3) KMS integration: if you want Redwood to encrypt customer keys with your KMS (recommended for regulated data), we need the key ARN and a short IAM policy. Monica has the KMS checklist attached.

Attachments: STREAM-Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx (checklist), kms-integration-guide.pdf (KMS preflight).

Proposed next actions (this week):
- Today: confirm org owners (who should get the first invites)
- Tomorrow: Monica issues invites and creates project skeleton
- Wednesday: 30-min runthrough to validate token scope and KMS access

If that cadence works I’ll calendar the Tue/Wed slots.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Roberts <amelia@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Hsu <kevin.hsu@streamlinehealth.com>
Date: 2025-07-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Org ignition: admin invites, API tokens, and KMS handoff

Thanks Jonas — sounds good. Quick answers from our side:

- Org owners: me (Amelia) and Kevin Hsu (security lead). Please add us both as owners.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS, key alias arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234. Kevin is CC'd and will confirm the precise policy.
- Token rotation: do you support short-lived tokens (1h) + a longer-lived service token for CI? We prefer short-lived where possible.

Also can you confirm what level of access the initial admin invites grant (full org owner vs admin)? We want to limit blast radius for the PoC.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll review and circle back.

Best,
Amelia Roberts
Head of Engineering
Streamline Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Roberts <amelia@streamlinehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Org ignition: admin invites, API tokens, and KMS handoff

Hi Amelia — thanks for the quick reply. I’ve sketched a lightweight implementation plan below (attached as STREAM-Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx):

Implementation plan (PoC lane) — 3 steps:

Step A — Admin invites (Day 0)
- I will send 3 invite types: Org Owner (2 people), Admin (2-3 people), Developer (4 people).
- Org Owner = full org scope: billing, model pinning, and rollout config. Admin = workspace-level config (projects, invites). Developer = API keys and runtime access only.
- For least privilege during PoC we’ll add Amelia and Kevin as Org Owners and add two Devs as Admins.

Step B — Project & service token (Day 1)
- Create a project called STREAM-POC.
- Seed a service token scoped to model:generate and embeddings:create (sample token attached: service-token-sample.json).
- We recommend a 30d rotation cadence for the service token; for CI we can provide ephemeral tokens (1h) via our token-issue API — Marcus will outline the API call.

Step C — KMS & secrets (Day 2)
- KMS preflight: confirm key ARN and principal (we need the KMS key policy to include redwood-service role).
- If you prefer Redwood-managed keys we can handle it; if you want customer-managed (recommended), we'll provide the minimal IAM policy in kms-integration-guide.pdf.

Risks & mitigations:
- If Kevin cannot add the KMS policy quickly we can proceed with Redwood-managed encryption and switch to customer KMS later without downtime.
- We will not seed production models or live data into the PoC project until token policies are approved.

Next steps:
1) Amelia/Kevin confirm owner names (reply)
2) I’ll send invites and project skeleton and upload the STREAM-Onboarding-Checklist to the shared drive
3) Marcus will post the sample API calls and token rotation pattern

Attachments: STREAM-Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx, kms-integration-guide.pdf, service-token-sample.json

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min runthrough for Wed 07/23 9:00am PT unless you prefer another slot.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Roberts <amelia@streamlinehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-21T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Org ignition: admin invites, API tokens, and KMS handoff

Adding a couple technical details on tokens and rotation so your infra/security team can review quickly: 

- Service token sample (attached) is a long-lived token intended for non-interactive CI only. It’s scoped by project and route; the sample limits calls to /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. We recommend a 30-day lifetime for PoC, with manual rotation if you want very strict control.
- Ephemeral token flow: we support token issuance via our token endpoint (POST /v1/tokens/issue) that returns JWT-style ephemeral keys with TTL up to 1h. Use case: human sessions, ephemeral CI jobs.
- KMS: when you provide the KMS key ARN please add this statement to the key policy (example in kms-integration-guide.pdf): "Allow: redwood-service-role to encrypt/decrypt". If you need we can publish a CloudFormation snippet.
- Rate limits: default PoC tier has 200 requests/min per project; if you need higher throughput for testing tell us and we can temporarily raise the limit.

Attachment: service-token-sample.json (sample), noted in the checklist.

I’ll be on the Wed runthrough to demo token issuance and show the ephemeral flow.

—Marcus Lin
Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick status: 
- I accepted the org owner invite and Kevin accepted the security invite.
- We created STREAM-POC and confirmed the initial developer list (I attached our internal access matrix to the shared drive).
- Kevin confirmed KMS key policy — he added redwood-service-role for Encrypt/Decrypt and will send the final policy snippet by EOD.
- We’d prefer ephemeral tokens for interactive testing and a short 7-30 day service token for CI; Kevin will validate on his end.

Confirming Wed 2025-07-23 09:00am PT works for the runthrough — calendar invite accepted. Please bring the token-issue demo and a quick walkthrough of where to find audit logs for key usage.

Appreciate the clear plan and attachments — looking forward to the runthrough.

Best,
Amelia Roberts
